name: Accordion
summary: Accordion displays a panel that the user can expand or collapse to show or hide content and control the complexity of a given view.
keywords: To organize related content within expandable groups/categories/sections.
To reduce scrolling or overall page length when displaying content in full isn't critical.
When you can't display all the content at once due to restricted screen space.

name: Avatar
summary: Avatar is a graphical element that you can use to represent a person, group, entity or communication channel.
keywords: To visually represent a person, group, entity or communication channel. The same image, initials, or placeholder image should appear for a given object instance throughout the experience.

name: Badge
summary: Badge is an alphanumeric annotation. It appears either inline or in the top-right corner of an element.
keywords: To communicate a non-interactive, system-driven change to the underlying component it anchors to, such as in tabs, pages and containers.
Typically, if you use a badge to indicate an unread notification, you'd hide the badge once the user addresses the notification. However, badges can remain persistent depending on the context.

name: Banner
summary: Banner is a type of notification that displays a message or provides feedback related to the user’s current workflow, spanning the page or container horizontally. It can communicate new information, errors, warnings or successful completion of a process or task.
keywords: To show a notification that applies to the user’s current task or workflow.

name: Border layout
summary: BorderLayout manages the top-level arrangement of your application, website or widget by positioning elements such as a footer, header and side navigation around the main content area. BorderLayout builds on top of GridLayout, defining five distinct regions, of which four surround the main content region. This layout is best for entire website pages or application screens with at least one additional region alongside the main area.
keywords: To manage the top-level layout of your application, or page, with at least one additional region alongside the main content area (e.g., for navigation or a footer).

name: Button
summary: Button is an interactive component that allows the user to execute an action. Button comes in three distinct appearances: solid, bordered, and transparent. These styles provide greater choice and flexibility for establishing hierarchy and affordance within a UI. You can display a button with or without a text description or icon.
keywords: To allow the user to execute an action, such as “submit”, “merge” or “upload”. Buttons are typically placed in components and contexts such as dialogs, cards and forms.

name: Calendar
summary: Calendar enables users to quickly navigate to and select one or a range of dates. Currently, all date-based controls need to be wrapped in a LocalizationProvider
keywords: Use the Calendar component when you need a versatile date selection tool that supports single, range, multiselect, or offset dates. This flexibility makes it ideal for financial applications, event scheduling, project timelines, and other scenarios where different date selection modes are necessary.

name: Card
summary: Card, LinkCard and InteractableCard are visually distinct content containers that display a snapshot of information about a single subject and act as an entry point for more detailed information.
keywords: To group related information with the same visual hierarchy.
To present a summary of a larger idea.
**Link cards:** to link to more detailed information.
**Interactable cards:** when you need a card to act as a button or when a group of cards needs to behave like a set of checkboxes or radio buttons.

name: Carousel
summary: Carousel can display single or multiple slides at a time. The navigation can be configured to be sequential as a group, where slide must be viewed in a specific order, or with a tablist, where users can access slides in any order.
keywords: To enable more than one piece of content to occupy the same space.
To navigate small amounts content, that are viewed in a linear sequence.
To position information near the top of the viewable area.

name: Chart
summary: Chart is a visually rich way to represent datasets, built on the Highcharts library to support a wide range of graph types and accessibility features while leveraging well-documented APIs for flexible integration and customization.

name: Checkbox
summary: Checkbox and CheckboxGroup allow users to select or deselect a specific option. A checkbox can stand alone to control a single option or form part of a checkbox group to control multiple options.
keywords: To present an independent choice that the user can select or deselect.
To present a list of independent options where the user can select any number of choices.

name: Collapsible
summary: Collapsible enables content to be either collapsed (hidden) or expanded (visible). It has two elements: a trigger and a panel whose visibility is controlled by the button.

name: Combo box
summary: ComboBox helps users to select an item from a large list of options without scrolling. The typeahead functionality makes this selection process quicker and easier, while reducing errors. Users see a list of options when they click on the component and then filter the list as they type. Once they’ve made a selection, it populates the field and the overlay list closes.
keywords: To display and select from a list of 10 or more options that don't need to be permanently visible to the user without selecting from a dropdown menu.
When only the selected value from a set of options needs to be visible once the selection is made.
If a workflow benefits from having a filter to quickly narrow down the available options.
If there are more than 100 options and you would like to prevent performance issues without virtualization.

name: Country symbol
summary: Country symbols display an icon that represents the flag of a country or territory. You can use country symbols individually or as a complete package. The country symbols are abstractly stylized, so users are more likely to recognize them at smaller sizes. Though we maintain their character within the circular form, we also provide rectangular "sharp" versions for every country symbol.
keywords: To display an icon that represents the flag of a country or territory.

name: Data grid
summary: Data grid is an interactive table for efficiently displaying data, supporting advanced features such as frozen columns, editable cells, custom cell renderers and flexible selection capabilities for rows and columns.
keywords: When you want to use the Salt theme with AG Grid.

name: Date input
summary: DateInputSingle and DateInputRange provide an editable field where users can enter a single date or a date range. Currently, all date-based controls need to be wrapped in a LocalizationProvider
keywords: Use the DateInputSingle component when you need to allow users to select a single date.
Use the DateInputRange component when you need to allow users to select a date range, between a start and end date.

name: Date picker
summary: DatePicker is composed of both a DateInput and Calendar controls. They allow users to select a single date, providing a flexible and intuitive way to make a selection.
keywords: Use a DatePicker component when you need a visual and intuitive interface for selecting single dates or date ranges, making it ideal for financial applications, event scheduling, and project management. In contrast, use a Dropdown when the dates are pre-determined, the selection is infrequent, or a compact interface is required, such as selecting a birth year or a specific month in a form.
A composable API enables you to use provided child components, such as DatePickerSingleInput and DatePickerSinglePanel.

name: Dialog
summary: Dialog is a window that opens over the application content, focusing the user’s attention on a particular task or piece of information. It communicates new information, errors, warnings or successful completion of a process.
keywords: To notify the user of critical information related to their current workflow that requires immediate action.

name: Divider
summary: Divider provides a thin, unobtrusive line for grouping elements and reinforcing visual hierarchy.
keywords: To provide visual separation between elements, regions and containers.

name: Drawer
summary: Drawer is an expandable panel that displays content and controls over the application's main information. It provides temporary access to additional or related options without fully navigating away from the current screen.
keywords: To reveal additional functionality or information contextual to on-screen content which the user can close when not required.
To display additional relevant functionality or information, such as a form or sidebar navigation, in a specific area of the screen.
To allow the user to show and hide additional relevant content.

name: Dropdown
summary: Dropdown allows the user to select from an overlaid vertical list of options. A selected value or values is displayed in the dropdown field, providing a screen space-efficient way of interacting with the list.
keywords: When a user needs the ability to choose one value from a set of five to 10 options.
When only the selected value from a set of options needs to be visible once the selection is made.

name: File drop zone
summary: FileDropZone provides a target area for users to drag and drop files, such as documents or images, and automatically upload them to the web application.
keywords: To enable users to upload single or multiple files from a native file browser.
To enable users to attach supporting files to a form.

name: Flex layout
summary: FlexLayout enables complex arrangement of UI elements within a container and facilitates responsive design by controlling the alignment, direction and size of items. Use it to arrange items in a row, evenly spaced and centered vertically, or to implement customized direction more complex than StackLayout, FlowLayout or SplitLayout. For additional control of the size and position of content, use FlexItem for each content item within FlexLayout.
keywords: When a complex layout cannot first be achieved using flow, stack and split layouts. However, if you are very familiar with CSS Flexbox, you may choose to use a flex layout from the start.

You want a layout that flows in a single dimension, where the dimension may change depending on other factors, such as viewport size. For example, in layouts where the direction and overflow behavior need to change depending on the viewport size or device.
For small-scale layout of components within a container or region within an application or webpage.

name: Flow layout
summary: FlowLayout is a simple mechanism that arranges UI elements in a horizontal order and responsively wraps them onto subsequent rows. It builds on top of FlexLayout and is best for small-scale layouts to display components in a responsive row, such as a row of metrics or a filter bar where fields wrap over multiple lines. For additional control of the size and position of content, use FlexItem for each content item inside a FlowLayout.
keywords: To build responsive layouts that wrap across multiple rows when there isn't enough space in the viewport.
For small-scale layouts within the application, such as a card in a dashboard displaying metrics or a header bar containing filter controls.

name: Form field
summary: FormField is a wrapper for user interface controls that are typically found in a form, such as Input, ComboBox or RadioButton. To make these controls accessible, you must provide them with a visible label, validation control, states and descriptive text elements.

name: Grid layout
summary: GridLayout enables complex arrangement of UI elements within a system of columns and rows to create an evenly distributed, responsive and organized user interface. Use it to position repeating widgets in the main content area, such as in a Dashboard. When combined with responsive breakpoints, you can configure GridLayout and GridItem to determine how content is displayed across different viewports and screen sizes.
keywords: When it's best to display your content using a configurable number of columns and rows, such as a form or a dashboard.
For content regions where you display blocks or groups of content alongside each other, such as the main content area of the application, Dialog, or Drawer.

When users will access the application or webpage across different viewport, screen or device sizes. GridLayout controls how to display the content and responsively organize across the different spaces, ensuring a reliable, usable experience.

name: Icon
summary: Icon is a visual representation of an application, a capability, a concept or a specific entity with meaning on an interface (e.g., a floppy disk to represent a save action). Icons help users to recognize and understand actions that transcend linguistic or cultural boundaries. The list of available icons is in the iconography foundation.
keywords: To aid recognition and help users make choices by providing context (e.g., an office phone number vs cell phone number in contact information).

name: Input
summary: Input provides an editable field for users to enter text using alphanumeric characters. It is ideal for short, freeform content and data entry.
keywords: To ask a user a subjective question to which user responses will vary and the length of their answer is likely to be less than a single line.

name: Kbd
summary: Kbd is a decorative element used to represent specific keyboard keys. It is typically embedded inside components (e.g., menu, table, button) or paragraph text, to communicate an associated keyboard shortcut or a user instruction.
keywords: To display keyboard shortcuts: Use Kbd to visually highlight keyboard keys or combinations (e.g., "Ctrl + S") in documentation.
Inline with instructions: When providing step-by-step instructions or help text that references keyboard actions.
In inputs: To show associated shortcuts for actions, such as “Save (Ctrl + S)” in a button or “Press Enter” in an input field.
In a menu: To associate with actions, such as the macOS Menu Bar or MS Taskbar.
To improve accessibility: When you want users to easily identify and understand available keyboard shortcuts.
For power users: Especially beneficial for users who are familiar with the application and frequently perform tasks at speed.

name: Link
summary: Link allows users to navigate to a different site or to other pages within the current site. You can use link on its own, or inline within or after a sentence.
keywords: To provide navigation to a page on the same or different site.
To link to documents, email addresses or phone numbers.
To send users to a specific section on the same page.
To provide users with more detailed information or assistance e.g., terms and conditions, help sections or contact information.

name: List box
summary: ListBox allows the user to select an item from an array of options, where selected items are visually distinct from non-selected items. To ensure efficient space usage, long lists of items are in a scrolling pane providing access to options not immediately visible.
keywords: To present a set of selectable options that allow users to make a choice for an onward action, such as filtering a data grid, selecting a country or assigning a task.

name: Localization provider
summary: LocalizationProvider configures the locale and date adapter for components with date objects.
keywords: When you use DatePicker, DateInput or Calendar components.
When you want to configure your own date adapter.
When you want to change the locale to non-US.
When you want to use a legacy data adapter, such as Moment as part of a migration journey to a maintained adapter.

name: Menu
summary: Menu is a container that presents a selection of choices or actions from which to choose. The user opens it with a customizable trigger, such as an interactive button, or an interaction, such as a keyboard shortcut or mouse right-click.
keywords: When you need to display a list of actions or options.
When you have limited space and need to display overflow action in a list.
When you need to display secondary or less important information and actions inside a trigger element.

name: Multiline input
summary: MultilineInput provides an editable text area where users can enter multiple lines of alphanumeric characters, while retaining visibility of what they've written.
keywords: Use a multiline input when asking a user a subjective question and the length of their answer is unknown. The input can give them plenty of space to answer the question and review the answer. If you can take an educated guess at the possible length of their answer, set the height accordingly—see the "Number of rows" example.

name: Navigation item
summary: NavigationItem allows users to navigate between discrete applications and/or web pages.
keywords: When you have multiple levels of navigation in your application or website.

We suggest first considering a horizontal group of navigation items for distinct webpages or applications. If you have multiple (more than eight) services to navigate to at a platform level, or have navigation across distinct apps, consider using a vertical group instead.
If you need your items to remain visible on scroll, we recommend displaying navigation items in a fixed app header (or header area).

name: Number input
summary: NumberInput displays a default numeric value that users can increase or decrease using the controls or with keyboard actions. Users can also manually enter a specific value. The component is useful for scenarios where users need to make small adjustments to a value within a well-defined range.
keywords: To adjust a value in small, precise increments or decrements, such as setting the quantity of items, adjusting a numerical setting, or specifying a time duration.
When the value has a clear minimum and maximum limit, and you want to prevent users from entering values outside this range.
When the input is purely numerical and does not require complex formatting.
If a user benefits from adjusting values without having to type them manually, especially on touch interfaces where typing can be cumbersome.
If there is a requirement to provide immediate visual feedback as the user adjusts the value, helping them understand the impact of their changes in real-time.

name: Overlay
summary: Overlay reveals supplementary content after the user clicks a UI trigger element. It remains active and open until dismissed by the user. It can contain interactive and focusable elements, such as buttons or links.
keywords: To expose interactive and essential elements within a tooltip to carry out in-context tasks.
For filter or dropdown panels that overlay content.
When acknowledgement on overlay content is needed. An overlay will only dismiss after user interaction.

name: Pagination
summary: Pagination allows users navigate easily between multiple pages of content. It enables users to jump to specific points within a set of results, helping to focus their attention and provide a sense of scale.
keywords: When presenting a large amount of content that may take time to load, or when users need to review and navigate to content that’s split across sequential pages.
To organize and present search results or data within a grid.

To provide a natural break point that allows users to determine if they’ve found what they need when viewing the results of a search or data query, or if they must navigate to another page or refine their initial query.
To enable users to reference specific pages within a set of results.

name: Panel
summary: Panel is a background that organizes content in an application. It uses color to reflect level of importance and convey visual hierarchy.
keywords: To organize and divide the application into clear content areas.
To create visual hierarchy within the application layout.
With the BorderLayout component to define the main content regions of your application with responsive behavior.

name: Parent-child layout
summary: Parent-childLayout provides a parent content area alongside a dependent child content area and responsively stacks them at a given breakpoint. It is used for interactions where selection in the parent (master) determines detail displayed in the child, such as navigation for a preferences dialog.
keywords: To organize content into two areas: a larger area, and a smaller area that controls the larger area.

name: Pill
summary: Pill is a small visual element that can contain text and an icon. Pills help label, filter or sort interactive content, allowing users to trigger actions or make selections.
keywords: To organize selections that don’t necessarily belong to the same category or need to be arranged in a certain way.
To trigger an immediate action such as filtering a view of content by a specific property.
To enable an action that could change depending on the context. In a messaging application, you could use pills to display predefined replies that change depending on the received message.

name: Progress
summary: Progress indicator gives the user a precise view of how long a system operation is taking. Use it when the action will last more than a second. Two variants are available to accommodate different layouts: CircularProgress and LinearProgress.
keywords: When it’s possible to determine the length of time remaining for a task or operation to complete. This will reassure the user that it is being processed.
To provide users with a visual indication of the status of an operation, or how much of a process is completed.
When the operation will take more than a second to complete, to reassure users that the operation is in progress.

name: Radio button
summary: RadioButton and RadioButtonGroup show a set of mutually exclusive options. Users can only select one radio button at a time. When selecting a new option, the previously selected option automatically clears. Radio buttons should be used to display a choice between two or more options, since users cannot clear a single radio button after selecting it.
keywords: When you have fewer than five options and only single selection is necessary.

name: Range date picker
summary: RangeDatePicker is composed of both a DateInput and Calendar controls. They enable users to select a date range that consists of a start and end date, offering a flexible and intuitive way to make a selection.
keywords: Use a DatePicker component when you need a visual and intuitive interface for selecting single dates or date ranges, making it ideal for financial applications, event scheduling, and project management. In contrast, use a Dropdown when the dates are pre-determined, the selection is infrequent, or a compact interface is required, such as selecting a birth year or a specific month in a form.

name: Range slider
summary: RangeSlider enables the selection of an interval within a range of values. It offers inline label positioning and can display marks under the track.
keywords: When selecting a range of numeric values or relative scale.
When the exact value does not matter (depending on the size of the predefined range), but an approximate interval is good enough.

name: Rating
summary: Rating component allows users to submit feedback and view average scores on a defined scale, reflecting your product, service or experience.
keywords: When you have to provide feedback or indicate your level of satisfaction with a product, service, or experience.
When there are at least 3 increments—this allows users to express a basic range of sentiment (poor, average, good).

name: Salt provider
summary: SaltProvider is a required component for changing the theme, mode, density and breakpoints of your application. Refer to the get started section for a step-by-step implementation guide.

name: Scrim
summary: Scrim is a temporary, translucent layer that makes underlying content less prominent.
keywords: To focus the user's attention on the content of an overlaying component within a specific viewport or content area.

name: Segmented button group
summary: SegmentedButtonGroup displays a set of actionable buttons that are flush with separators.
keywords: Use the segmented button group to display a list of actionable buttons, flush with separators between them.

name: Semantic icon provider
summary: SemanticIconProvider centralizes icon management and customization with Salt. It allows flexible configuration of icons and ensures consistent usage across your application.

name: Skip link
summary: SkipLink allows screen reader and keyboard users to bypass menus and jump directly into the main content. This removes accessibility barriers by reducing keystroke repetition and streamlining navigation.
keywords: Bypass repetitive navigation or elements at the top of a page, providing direct access to the main content.
Ensure screen reader and keyboard users can efficiently reach key sections of your web application.
Prevent users from repeatedly hearing header and navigation content on every page before accessing the main content.

name: Slider
summary: Slider enables the selection of a single value within a range of values. It offers inline label positioning and can display marks under the track.
keywords: When selecting a single value, range of numeric values or relative scale.
When the exact value does not matter (depending on the size of the predefined range), but an approximate value is good enough.
When changes are applied for immediate feedback, e.g., changing the volume on an audio or video player.

name: Spinner
summary: Spinner is a visual representation of a process taking indeterminate time to complete. Triggers include automated system processes and user actions. It can also indicate content loading. Displaying a spinner reassures the user that the system is still working, especially when the operation takes longer than one second.
keywords: To indicate that content is loading and reassure the user that the system is still working.
For actions that you expect will take 1–9 seconds to load or for processes that will take an indeterminate amount of time to complete.

name: Split layout
summary: SplitLayout is a simple mechanism which arranges UI elements at opposite ends of a container. Use it with vertical or horizontal orientation, to provide visual hierarchy for controls such as buttons or toolbars.
keywords: If you need two defined areas at the opposite horizontal ends of a container, for example, if you need two button bar components in a header.

name: Splitter
summary: Splitter allows users to customize their workspace layout by interactively adjusting the boundaries between two or more panels, either horizontally or vertically, depending on the orientation and arrangement of the panels.

name: Stack layout
summary: StackLayout is a simple mechanism to arrange UI elements in a line, either horizontally or vertically. It builds on the FlexLayout component and is best for small-scale layouts where displaying components in a single row or column is necessary. It may benefit from supported visual separators, such as a row of charts or a scrolling side panel comprising multiple sections. For additional control of the size and position of content, use FlexItem for each content item inside StackLayout.
keywords: When you need a layout that's consistently horizontal or vertical. If there isn't enough space in the main axis, scrolling the content is acceptable.
For small-scale layouts within the application, such as a stack of cards or charts or a vertical side panel with visually distinct sections.
To change the layout’s direction depending on breakpoints or add visual separation using the stack layout separators.

name: Static list
summary: StaticList manages the layout of non-interactive list items, providing a structured and composable way to display content. It's ideal for use in checkout baskets and patterns such as file upload.
keywords: To present a set of static list items. It can be used with a FileDropZone to show the list of files added. It can also be used to create a shopping cart list.

name: Status indicator
summary: StatusIndicator is a specialized icon to show info, warning, error or success. Use on its own or within another component (e.g., Tooltip) to help convey a message.
keywords: Use the info indicator when you need to highlight general information.
Use the error indicator when communicating a critical issue preventing the user from continuing or completing an action.
Use the warning indicator to inform users of an issue or potential issue related to their current task. Use this for issues that don't prevent the user from continuing or completing their task.
Use the success indicator to confirm that a user's action is successful.

name: Stepper
summary: Stepper communicates user progress through a linear process. It gives context about where they are, which steps are completed, how many steps are remaining, and whether errors or warnings have occurred.
keywords: When there are separate steps within a process, such as a wizard or a multi-step form.
When you want to split a process into distinct, bite-sized sections that are less daunting than lengthy forms.

name: Switch
summary: Switch is a binary control used as a toggle between two different states. When engaged, the thumb travels within the track to indicate change of state. Use it for adjusting settings, preferences or actions within an application or system.
keywords: To present an instantaneous, binary choice between two options that doesn’t require the user to submit or confirm the action. The corresponding action takes effect immediately.
To control a critical action that may require confirmation from the user before applying it. This delay is usually intentional, ensuring that users don't accidentally make unwanted changes.

name: System status
summary: SystemStatus communicates essential platform-wide information, such as maintenance or outage alerts. These messages are displayed to be noticed immediately, prompting users to consider taking action based on four severity levels (with corresponding icons and colors): info, success, warning and error.
keywords: To inform users about critical system-wide issues, security updates or vulnerabilities that require immediate attention.
To notify users about new system-wide features or enhancements.
To alert users about planned maintenance schedules and potential service disruptions affecting the entire platform.

name: Table
summary: Table is a basic HTML component intended for simple but structured tabular data display.
keywords: When you need to present data in a structured, tableau format.

name: Tabs
summary: Tabs allow users to move between different views of related content without leave the current page. A tab strip includes at least two tabs. Only one tab is actively engaged at a time and is differentiated from inactive tabs by a colored indicator either on the top or bottom edge of the tab, depending on the variant. Tab strips can cover the full width of the page or be limited to content areas within components such as dialogs, cards, and drawers.
keywords: Use tabs to organize logically related but mutually exclusive content on a single page.
Use tabs to prevent users from navigating to another page to complete a task.

name: Tag
summary: Tag displays metadata categorizing or grouping content in an application. They are read-only and do not interfere with page interactions but use categorical colors to draw attention. Tags appear as stylized elements with text, optionally accompanied by an icon to reinforce their meaning.
keywords: For displaying categories in a catalogue or within a group.
To display non-interactive data on a page.

name: Text
summary: Text component facilitates use of Salt typography styles throughout a product or application, ensuring consistency and unified look and feel. It includes attributes such as font size, weight, letter spacing, line height and decoration.

name: Toast
summary: Toast displays a small pop-up notification with short feedback in response to a user action. It can also contextualize a system event in a workflow or application outside the user’s current focus. Toasts communicate new information, errors, warnings or successful completion of a process.
keywords: To notify users of an event that’s occurred in a peripheral application or workflow. The user should notice the toasts without disrupting their experience or requiring immediate action.
To communicate low-priority information caused by events. Toasts usually don’t require feedback from the user.
To communicate information from a workflow external to the user’s current task or view. Toasts are in an un-intrusive location on an interface.

To show system-generated alerts, independent of the user’s actions. These toasts are persistent and must allow the user to either take action or dismiss them. Toasts can contain customizable content, such as actionable buttons.

name: Toggle button
summary: ToggleButton allows users to switch states, typically representing on/off or active/inactive status. The corresponding action takes effect immediately. With ToggleButtonGroup, users can make a single choice from a set of related commands, with only one option selected at a time.
keywords: To make a single selection when switching between opposing yet mutually exclusive options.
To visually prioritize options higher than RadioButton or Switch.

name: Tokenized input
summary: TokenizedInput provides a field for text entry that is converted into a pill once the user enters a delimiting character (e.g., comma, semicolon or space).
keywords: The component is typically used in a form. It’s ideal for fields that can contain multiple, specific values related to a single topic or context—and these values can be removed quickly and in their entirety. You would use the component, for example, in a field for email addresses or a fast field for a cash ticket.

name: Tooltip
summary: Tooltip is a non-modal overlay that appears on hover or focus. Initially hidden, it provides concise, text-only content related to the associated interactive element. It also typically offers supplementary, non-essential information without disturbing the user workflow.
keywords: When you want to display a brief message to the user that provides additional information about an interactive UI element.

name: Tree
summary: Tree displays hierarchical data as an expandable and collapsible structure. Users can navigate nested items and optionally select one or more nodes.
keywords: To display hierarchical data with parent-child relationships, such as file systems, organizational structures or category taxonomies.
When users need to explore a multi-level hierarchy, browse nested levels and optionally select items, while allowing multiple branches to remain open.

name: Vertical navigation
summary: VerticalNavigation allows users to move between distinct applications and web pages.
keywords: When you have multiple levels of navigation in your application or website.

We suggest first considering a horizontal group of navigation items for distinct webpages or applications. If you have multiple (more than eight) services to navigate to at a platform level, or have navigation across distinct apps, consider using a vertical group instead.
If you need your items to remain visible on scroll, we recommend displaying navigation items in a fixed app header (or header area).

name: AccessibleIcon
summary: Accessible icon for accessibility concepts such as wheelchair, support, wcag.

name: AccessibleSolidIcon
summary: Accessible solid icon for accessibility concepts such as wheelchair, support, wcag.

name: AddIcon
summary: Add icon for organize concepts such as create, plus, new.

name: AddDocumentIcon
summary: Add Document icon for documents concepts such as upload, file, generate.

name: AddDocumentSolidIcon
summary: Add Document solid icon for documents concepts such as upload, file, generate.

name: AddToGridIcon
summary: Add To Grid icon for organize concepts such as insert, layout.

name: AddToGridSolidIcon
summary: Add To Grid solid icon for organize concepts such as insert, layout.

name: AddUserIcon
summary: Add User icon for people concepts such as invite, plus, new.

name: AnnouncementIcon

name: About Salt
summary: Salt is the J.P. Morgan design system, an open-source solution for building exceptional products and digital experiences in financial services and other industries.

name: Accordion
summary: For assistive technologies, the visible label on a control usually acts as the accessible name.

name: Accordion
summary: By default, Accordion is a single element the user can expand or collapse to show or hide content within a panel.

name: Accordion
summary: To organize related content within expandable groups/categories/sections.

name: Actionable characteristic
summary: Actionable tokens define the colors and styles for actionable components, making elements that can perform actions—such as buttons—distinct and easy to identify. Actionable is organized by sentiment values (accented, caution, positive, negative) and emphasis levels (bold, subtle), allowing you to convey the importance or nature of an action.

name: Analytical dashboard
summary:
An analytical dashboard enables users to analyze trends, patterns and metrics effectively. You can use this to present data in a hierarchical and intuitive manner.

The mock-ups displayed in this pattern are available as [templates](https://www.figma.com/file/O3FYUQYXLosmEuZc0T30Qo/Analytical-Dashboard-Pattern?type=design&node-id=1288-5747&mode=design&t=Pu46NKEwCeMRSjPD-0) in Figma _(J.P. Morgan employees only)_.

name: Announcement dialog
summary: An announcement dialog promotes new features and can provide users with access to onward action, such as installing version updates.

name: App header
summary: An app header is a consistently available element that sits at the top of every application interface. It contains a brand logo or mark and application-wide functionality, including navigation and utility actions.

name: Avatar
summary: Exclude decorative avatars (avatars that repeat the information already expressed by the accompanying text) from screen reader access to avoid repetition. If you're adding an avatar for decorative purposes, use aria-hidden to exclude its label from the screen reader.

name: Avatar
summary: You can pass an image as the avatar image using the src prop.

name: Avatar
summary: To visually represent a person, group, entity or communication channel. The same image, initials, or placeholder image should appear for a given object instance throughout the experience.

name: Badge
summary: When you've attached a badge to a child component, and that component receives focus, ensure the focusable element has an aria-label or aria-labelledby attribute that describes the badge, such as "9 notifications." - When the user navigates to an inline badge, the screen reader automatically announces the contents of the badge. Use aria-label to provide more context to the badge contents if needed.

name: Badge
summary: The Badge is anchored to the top-right corner when attached to a child component such as a button. As the number of alphanumeric characters increases, the badge width expands but stays in the same place.

name: Badge
summary: If a numeric annotation exceeds the max value passed as a prop, there will be a plus (+) after the max value stated. If you don't pass a max value to the component, it will truncate the value after three digits displaying 999+ for any values over 999.

name: Banner
summary: Check and test any focusable elements included in the banner content.

name: Banner
summary: The static banner displays information to the user, has no interactive elements, and is nonfunctional.

name: Banner
summary: Always position the banner component in the main content area or in the related container component. It should sit directly below the navigation and span the page or container horizontally.

name: Border layout
summary: When building a page layout, apply semantic HTML. This means using the correct HTML elements for their intended purpose as much as possible.

name: Border layout
summary: You can set BorderLayout to display five regions: North, East, South, West and Center. You must display at least one region alongside the Center region in the layout.

name: Border layout
summary: To manage the top-level layout of your application, or page, with at least one additional region alongside the main content area (e.g., for navigation or a footer).

name: Border style
summary: The border style foundation provides a standardized set of design tokens to ensure consistent border styles across all components and patterns.

name: Breadcrumbs
summary: Breadcrumbs are a secondary navigation pattern that helps users keep track of their current location within a hierarchy. It provides a space-efficient means of allowing quick navigation to previous levels.

name: Breakpoints
summary: Responsive design utilizes breakpoints to adapt UI layouts and optimize presentation of information across different application resolutions and orientations. This approach enhances user experience by ensuring content remains readable and accessible.

name: Button
summary: When a button has both an icon and text, use aria-hidden on the icon so that screen readers don't announce its text.

name: Button
summary: The accented button is the main button set for your UI. It is typically used for the core actions in your workflow. Three different appearances are available based on the prominence required for the actions.

name: Button
summary: Keep the text description short, ideally one to three words and no more than five. If you’re including an icon with the text, use no more than three words.

name: Button bar
summary: A button bar displays possible actions for users to take when they reach the end of a task. You can use it to provide consistent presentation of button types and orders within pages or dialogs across your applications.

name: Calendar
summary: The Calendar component is typically not used on its own but is composed with other components to build more user-friendly components such as DatePicker.

name: Calendar
summary: When the selectionVariant prop is set to "single", the Calendar component allows users to select only a single date, providing a straightforward and focused date selection experience.

name: Calendar
summary: To use the Calendar component, compose it with the provided children.

name: Card
summary: To meet accessibility standards, the boundaries of a user interface component are only subject to the 3:1 contrast minimum if they serve to identify the components purpose.

name: Card
summary: By default, the card component does not have any interactive or focusable elements.

name: Card
summary: Cards may include text, images, or interactive elements. Make sure the content aligns with your use case, keeping it clear and easy to read. Avoid overcrowding cards with excessive content, actions, or links embedded in the text.

name: Carousel
summary: Avoid using infographics, maps, or charts as images, and do not use images of text.

name: Carousel
summary: Carousel is a pre-defined composition of Salt components that uses the Embla API.

name: Carousel
summary: Carousels offer two types of navigation, sequential and non-sequential.

name: Categorical colors
summary: Salt’s categorical palette is designed for data visualization and components that represent distinct categories, featuring 20 unique colors and their corresponding ramps.

name: Category characteristic
summary: Category tokens provide a palette of distinct colors for differentiating groups within your interface, such as in data visualizations or components that support content grouping. While the colors themselves do not imply meaning, meaning can be associated to each category within the context of your application.

name: Chart
summary: Highcharts provides an accessibility module that enhances the accessibility of charts.

name: Chart
summary: To ensure the presentation is accessible, line or fill patterns can be applied to the chart (see Patterns and Fills for details). Use the "Show patterns" switch to toggle patterns.

name: Chart
summary: Install the following dependencies: - highcharts - version 10.2.0 specifically, or version 11+ - highcharts-react-official - @salt-ds/highcharts-theme

name: Chart accessibility
summary: Charts rely on visual elements to make complex data easier to understand, so it’s essential they are accessible to everyone. Ground your chart design and implementation in the WCAG POUR principles: - **Perceivable**: Text equivalents (caption, summary), accessible data table, sufficient contrast, labels/patterns/markers instead of color alone.

name: Chart anatomy
summary: Understanding the principles of chart anatomy is important to learning how the different parts of Salt charts work.

name: Chart types
summary: Data visualization presents information in a visual form that’s easy to understand. When applied to dense and complex datasets, it aids in highlighting trends and patterns.

name: Checkbox
summary: If you're using a checkbox without a text description, pass an aria-label to the checkbox that describes its purpose.

name: Checkbox
summary: A single checkbox can be either selected or deselected.

name: Checkbox
summary: To present an independent choice that the user can select or deselect.

name: Collapsible
summary: If focus is above the collapsible trigger, Tab moves focus to the trigger.

name: Collapsible
summary: Collapsible is a component that allows you to show or hide content with a click. It can be used to create expandable sections in your UI.

name: Collapsible
summary: To import Collapsible and related components from the core Salt package, use:

name: Color and pattern
summary: Color is a valuable tool that helps effectively present data in your visualization. Using color correctly guides users’ attention and supports their understanding and interpretation of data.

name: Combo box
summary: If the combo box is single-select and if focus is above the combo box, Tab sets focus on the component. When focused, combo box has a visible text cursor and the list is opened.

name: Combo box
summary: By default, a single item can be selected from the combo box options. The selected option is displayed in the input field.

name: Combo box
summary: To display and select from a list of 10 or more options that don't need to be permanently visible to the user without selecting from a dropdown menu.

name: Components
summary: Our components are built with accessibility in mind. Each one has comprehensive supporting documentation with usage guidance, examples and props.

name: Contact details
summary: Contact details display communication information for a person, company, distribution list or individual channel. This can include a name, a phone number or email address.

name: Container characteristic
summary: Container tokens define the background and structure of interface elements, helping to group related content and create visual hierarchy. Each variant—primary, secondary, and tertiary—aligns with theme background colors to support different levels of emphasis. Containers can also include borders and shadows, with shadow options provided by the Overlayable characteristic, to further distinguish and elevate content within your layout.
keywords: Styling a container as a drop target

name: Content characteristic
summary: Content tokens define the standard foreground colors for all text and icons within Salt, ensuring clarity and consistency across your interface. Available in variants such as primary, secondary, accent, and attention, these tokens should be applied to all foreground elements unless another characteristic—like actionable—takes precedence for interactive states. Using content tokens appropriately helps maintain visual harmony and supports accessibility throughout your application.

name: Content status
summary: A content status provides information about content in a container component of an application. It remains onscreen until a situation resolves or the user takes action, making it a great tool for communication and guidance.

name: Country symbol
summary: If you're using a country symbol for decorative purposes, and the country is named in accompanying text, hide its label from screen readers to avoid repetition. To hide the label, pass aria-hidden=”true”.

name: Country symbol
summary: We include all countries and subdivisions that appear in the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 3166-1 standard. Though we use the country names, alpha-2 codes and corresponding alphabetical order from ISO, our symbols derive from whichever flag the official United Nations list provides for each country. Of the 249 countries currently in the ISO list, 193 are sovereign states with UN membership. We also include the EU symbol, due to its economic importance.

name: Country symbol
summary: To reduce the core package's bundle size, country symbols are in a separate package that you should first install using: npm install @salt-ds/countries or yarn add @salt-ds/countries

name: Country symbols
summary: Country symbols represent a specific place and are used in contexts where geographical identification is necessary. They are essentially icons that are visually indicative of a country or territory. All country symbols are available in both circle and rectangle shapes.

name: Cursor
summary: The cursor foundation controls how the cursor appears when positioned over or interacting with a component. This behavior is only relevant for web browsers and operating systems that display cursors in the user interface.

name: Data grid
summary: This package has no accessibility guidance.

name: Data grid
summary: Applies the default look when applying the Salt theme.

name: Data grid
summary: When you want to use the Salt theme with AG Grid.

name: Date input
summary: Wrap DateInputSingle and DateInputRange in FormField to provide the field with a visible label, help text, and a status message for validation feedback. This will ensure it complies with accessibility guidelines. You can find more information in the W3C form instructions.

name: Date input
summary: An uncontrolled DateInputSingle component allows users to select a single date without the need for explicit state management in the parent component. The component internally manages the date value, making it ideal for simple forms where the date input does not need to be programmatically controlled or monitored.

name: Date input
summary: To avoid misleading users, set the width of the input to correlate with the length of the expected answer. For example, an input for a three-digit value shouldn't be wide enough to accommodate a sentence worth of characters. See forms pattern for more information on layout.

name: Date picker
summary: Wrap DatePicker in FormField to provide the field with a visible label, help text, and a status message for validation feedback. This will ensure it complies with accessibility guidelines. You can find more information in the W3C form instructions.

name: Date picker
summary: All date components requires LocalizationProvider to be set up in your application.

name: Date picker
summary: DatePicker provides a context to the children contained within it and a composable API that enables you to create your own date picker controls.

name: Density
summary: Density relates to the amount of content that can fit on a screen based on the size and spacing of components. When building a product with Salt, select the density that best suits your use case. All components, spacing, and typographic elements will align and remain proportionate regardless of the density you choose.

name: Design tokens
summary: Salt styles its components and patterns using design tokens. Design tokens are name and value pairings that capture small, repeatable design choices—such as colors, fonts, and spacing—and are essential for storing key style attributes in a design system. They help maintain consistency across platforms and applications, making it easier to update and maintain a cohesive look throughout your products.

name: Designing with Salt Figma libraries
summary: Salt provides a comprehensive set of components and styles, which include themes, typography, color palettes, iconography and more. Designers can use the components as they are, out of the box, or adapt them to suit the needs of a business or application.
keywords: Step 4: Search for Salt DS libraries
Step 5: Add library to your file

name: Developing with Salt
summary: Learn how to use Salt's UI components in your React web applications.

name: Dialog
summary: Provide an accessible name for dialogs by using the visible DialogHeader (recommended) or, if design constraints prevent this, apply an aria-label attribute directly to the Dialog to meet WCAG 4.1.2 requirements.

name: Dialog
summary: The dialog displays with a header, content area, and action bar. The component is modal, meaning it prevents interaction with the rest of the UI while open and must be addressed by clicking one of the action buttons or dismissing with the close button in DialogHeader. If the content of the dialog extends beyond the end of the screen, the DialogContent area will become scrollable.

name: Dialog
summary: Dialogs are interruptive by nature and should be used sparingly. Use dialogs to present or gather critical information that requires immediate action, whether it’s directly or indirectly part of the user’s current task. For example, a warning dialog that appears when a document is closed without being saved—and asks how the user wishes to proceed—is indirectly related to the user’s task.

name: Divider
summary: Divider has a role of separator and is sometimes announced by screen readers as "Horizontal Splitter". If you're adding a divider for decorative purposes, pass aria-hidden="true" to make screen readers skip it.

name: Divider
summary: Divider has three variants: primary, secondary and tertiary. The default variant is primary. You can use the variant prop to change

name: Divider
summary: To provide visual separation between elements, regions and containers.

name: Drawer
summary: If focus is on the trigger element, this action activates the element and opens the drawer. Focus doesn't leave the drawer.

name: Drawer
summary: By default, a drawer anchors to the left edge of the screen and has variant="primary".

name: Drawer
summary: Drawers cover the entire height of the viewport and are always modal. This means that the content behind them is inert and can't be interacted with. A Scrim is used to visually obscure the content behind the drawer.

name: Dropdown
summary: If focus is above the dropdown, Tab sets focus on the component. When focused, dropdown has a visible text cursor and the list is opened.

name: Dropdown
summary: Users can select a single item from the dropdown options.

name: Dropdown
summary: When a user needs the ability to choose one value from a set of five to 10 options.

name: Duration
summary: Duration represents the time between a user performing an action and the system giving feedback. It’s essential to indicate to users that something is happening when they interact with an element. Consistency in timing provides user comfort and can increase trust in a system. The duration should match the significance of the animated element or information.

name: Editable characteristic
summary: Editable tokens specify the colors and styles for components that support data entry and modification. This characteristic is used for input controls like text fields, where users can write or edit information. Editable tokens ensure that these components are visually distinct and easy to identify, often accompanied by labels to guide user interaction and support clear, accessible data entry.

name: Extended styling
summary: Salt provides you with options which enable you to customize your UI for specific use cases, whilst keeping everything consistent and maintainable. You can adjust densities, switch themes, and choose between light and dark modes. Most components offer props that help to establish clear hierarchy or alter prominence, with predefined variants and appearances to fit different situations. There are also semantic color options for sentiment, status, and categories—giving you plenty of flexibility without needing to override.

name: Feedback
summary: We appreciate your thoughts and feedback on any content in the Salt foundations. Please contact us if you have any comments or questions.

name: Feedback
summary: If you need to expand the pattern or share feedback with us, please contact the team.

name: File drop zone
summary: Tab sets focus to the **'Browse files'** button. If focus is in the file drop zone, Tab sets focus to the next focusable component in the tab order.

name: File drop zone
summary: This component allows users to upload files they've selected from the native file browser interface or dragged-and-dropped. The component automatically uploads the files to your web application.

name: File drop zone
summary: To enable users to upload single or multiple files from a native file browser.

name: File upload
summary: A file upload allows users to transfer one or multiple files from an external source to the web application. This pattern is commonly embedded in forms or as a standalone element.

name: Flex layout
summary: When building a layout for part of a page using FlexLayout, apply semantic HTML. This means using the correct HTML elements for their intended purpose as much as possible.

name: Flex layout
summary: By default, FlexLayout displays items along the horizontal axis in a row, aligned to the start of the container. The dimensions of the layout (height or width) are driven by the items contained within it.

name: Flex layout
summary: When a complex layout cannot first be achieved using flow, stack and split layouts. However, if you are very familiar with CSS Flexbox, you may choose to use a flex layout from the start.

name: Flow layout
summary: When building a sub-section of a page using a flow layout, apply semantic HTML, This means using the correct HTML elements for their intended purpose as much as possible.

name: Flow layout
summary: A flow layout displays items in a row that will responsively wrap onto a new line.

name: Flow layout
summary: To build responsive layouts that wrap across multiple rows when there isn't enough space in the viewport.

name: Form field
summary: All keyboard interactions are supplied by the underlying wrapped components, rather than the FormField component.

name: Form field
summary: All examples demonstrate Salt form controls inside the form field, including Input, Checkbox and RadioButton. These components are available as part of the Salt component library in addition to FormField.
keywords: Grouped with left aligned label placement
Grouped with top aligned label placement
Grouped with right aligned label placement

name: Form field
summary: We highly recommend using the FormFieldLabel and FormFieldHelperText components within the form field to provide your form elements with the descriptive label and validation feedback required to ensure ADA compliance.

name: Forms
summary: A form allows you to capture data, gather opinions and receive information in a consistent format. This pattern provides guidelines for creating forms that are flexible to business domain, user experience and channel.

name: Foundations
summary: Foundations are the fundamental principles that guide the creation of a cohesive design language, enabling you to build products that are easy to use and visually appealing.

name: Get started
summary: Follow our step-by-step guides to design and develop accessible, responsive, best-in-class user experiences with Salt.

name: Glossary
summary: Learn what technical terms for design and development mean specifically in the context of Salt. Note that the order of this glossary of definitions is purposefully not alphabetical but is sequenced according to the Salt site navigation, so that related terms appear next to similar concepts.

name: Grid layout
summary: When building a page layout, apply semantic HTML. This means using the correct HTML elements for their intended purpose as much as possible.

name: Grid layout
summary: GridLayout defaults to a 12-column grid with one row.

name: Grid layout
summary: When it's best to display your content using a configurable number of columns and rows, such as a form or a dashboard.

name: Header block
summary: Header block is a standardized header for container components and application regions, used to display various text elements depending on scenarios. Headings can also display accent and status to highlight messaging.

name: How to read semantic tokens
summary: Salt organizes semantic tokens within the characteristic layer, allowing components and patterns to reference them directly. Understanding semantic characteristics involves learning how to interpret token names, making it easier to find and apply the right token in both design and code.

name: Icon
summary: Exclude decorative icons (icons that repeat the information already expressed by the accompanied text) from screen reader access to avoid repetition. If you're adding an icon for decorative purposes, pass aria-hidden=”true” to exclude its label from the screen reader.

name: Icon
summary: You should individually import and use from the @salt-ds/icons package.

name: Icon
summary: To aid recognition and help users make choices by providing context (e.g., an office phone number vs cell phone number in contact information).

name: Icons
summary: Icons are simplified visual representations of a specific action, object or concept.

name: Indication
summary: The indication pattern provides a starting point for designers to apply common indication scenarios, with consideration for color, iconography and recommended labeling guidelines.

name: Input
summary: Wrap Input in FormField to provide the field with a visible label, help text, and a status message for validation feedback. This will ensure it complies with accessibility guidelines. You can find more information in the W3C form instructions.

name: Input
summary: Input is a single-line text field that accepts user input. It can be used in forms, search bars, or anywhere you need to capture user input.

name: Input
summary: To avoid misleading users, set the width to correlate to the length of the answer you’re expecting. For example, an input for a three-digit value shouldn't be wide enough to accommodate a sentence worth of characters. See forms pattern for more information on layout.

name: International address form
summary:
An international address form gives users a set of form fields to input address information for specific countries. The form displays relevant fields for a user-selected location.

The pattern aims to accommodate users worldwide, but your team may be able to take further steps that fall outside its scope. For example, check with your tech partners if it's possible to detect user location and automatically adjust the form.

Future versions of this pattern will cover the use of APIs, autocompletion and enhanced support for more locations.

name: International phone number
summary:
An international phone number input gives users a set of form fields to input phone number information for specific countries.

The pattern is a form that displays a relevant phone number field for a user-selected location. You can use it to provide consistent design when implementing International Phone Number Input interactions across your applications.

We provide design guidance on how you can use Salt form control components to achieve the pattern. Your team can take further steps that fall outside its scope. For example, check with your tech partners if it’s possible to autodetect user location using data that can support auto-generating number placeholders. You can also check if it's possible to save the entered number when the user changes the country.

name: JPM brand characteristic tokens
summary: Accent highlights key elements by applying a theme's dominant color, helping important components—like active tabs or headings—stand out and draw attention.

name: JPM brand colors
summary: These are the JPM brand theme colors, approved for digital use by the brand team. The palette supports clear communication, visual hierarchy, and product differentiation, while ensuring a cohesive and accessible experience across Salt applications.

name: Kbd
summary: Screen readers will announce Kbd content as plain text.

name: Kbd
summary: Kbd supports multiple background color variants: primary, secondary, and tertiary. The primary variant is set by default. These variants help match different UI backgrounds and provide varying levels of visual emphasis, depending on how important the shortcuts are in a given scenario.

name: Kbd
summary: To display keyboard shortcuts: Use Kbd to visually highlight keyboard keys or combinations (e.g., "Ctrl + S") in documentation.

name: Keyboard shortcuts
summary: Keyboard shortcuts allow users to execute actions, that are usually performed with a mouse or trackpad, using a keyboard. They increase the efficiency and productivity of users who primarily rely on their keyboard when interacting with applications.
keywords: Choosing a container for the keyboard shortcuts
Integrating third party keyboard shortcut libraries

name: Layout grid
summary: A layout grid provides a consistent structure for Salt user interfaces, organizing content into columns separated by gutters and framed by margins. The grid adapts to different screen sizes, with column number and width changing by density and breakpoint. This ensures layouts remain clear, balanced, and accessible across devices.

name: Legacy (UITK) characteristics tokens
summary: Accent highlights key elements by applying a theme's dominant color, helping important components—like active tabs or headings—stand out and draw attention.

name: Legacy (UITK) colors
summary: Salt recommends using the JPM brand theme for your product, as the legacy (UITK) color palette is not aligned with current brand standards and may present accessibility challenges. The legacy palette is provided primarily to support migration from UI Toolkit to Salt, and should only be used when necessary for compatibility.

name: Link
summary: Screen reader users will use the Tab key to jump from link to link or pull up a list of links on a page. Avoid using the same link text to link to different content and ensure that links make sense out of context.

name: Link
summary: By default, a link will only navigate the user within the same tab, replacing the page where the user followed the link.

name: Link
summary: To provide navigation to a page on the same or different site.

name: List box
summary: If focus is above the list, Tab moves focus to one of the following options depending on previous user interaction: - The last selected option - The first option in the list If focus is below the list, this action moves focus to one of the following options depending on previous user interaction: - The last selected option - The last option in the list When focus is on an option, this action selects the option and if the list box is single-select deselects the previously selected option, if any.

name: List box
summary: The default list allows a user to make a single selection from the options available.

name: List box
summary: To present a set of selectable options that allow users to make a choice for an onward action, such as filtering a data grid, selecting a country or assigning a task.

name: List builder
summary: A list builder allows users to create a bespoke list of items from an original list, also known as a pick list, adding or removing items as required. Users can filter the items by using the filter input field.

name: List filtering
summary: When searching through a list, a filter enables users to specify criteria and only show relevant options. This pattern introduces the filter behavior of Salt components where a list is used.

name: Localization provider
summary: This component has no accessibility guidance.

name: Localization provider
summary: To integrate your date framework with Salt components and enable support for locales or timezones, defining a date adapter is essential. Salt provides date adapters for the most popular date frameworks, which you can extend or use as a foundation to create your own custom adapter.

name: Localization provider
summary: Wrap your application with typically one LocalizationProvider to define the date adapter for date based controls.

name: Menu
summary: If focus is on a menu item, Tab closes the menu and moves focus to the next focusable element in the tab order.

name: Menu
summary: Clicking on the menu trigger will display a list of actions that the user can take.

name: Menu
summary: Menu items should relate to the interactive element or interaction that triggers the menu.

name: Menu button
summary: A menu button expands to reveal numerous contextual options when there's limited space to display them. The items within the menu are often less frequently used and don't require constant display within the interface.

name: Metric
summary: A metric displays an important number value prominently. You can add indicators or labels to help provide context to the presented value.

name: Modes
summary: Modes enable the color palette to change from light to dark, providing the flexibility to choose an option that best fits a preference or need. Choosing a suitable mode can improve accessibility, reduce eye strain in low-light conditions and increase reading speed.

name: Multiline input
summary: Wrap MultilineInput in FormField to provide the field with a visible label, help text and a status message for validation feedback. This will ensure it complies with accessibility guidelines. You can find more information in the W3C form instructions.

name: Multiline input
summary: MultilineInput is a text input field that allows the user to enter multiple lines of text. Values entered into the multiline input wrap based on the width of the component. By default, the component presents three rows of text at a time.

name: Multiline input
summary: Use a multiline input when asking a user a subjective question and the length of their answer is unknown. The input can give them plenty of space to answer the question and review the answer. If you can take an educated guess at the possible length of their answer, set the height accordingly—see the "Number of rows" example.

name: Navigable characteristic
summary: The Navigable characteristic defines the colors and styles for components that support navigation, such as Tabs, Vertical Navigation or Navigation Item. These components enable users to switch between sections, pages, or data sets and change context easily. The tokens highlighted in this guide ensure navigation elements are visually clear and consistent, making it easy for users to move through different parts of the interface.

name: Navigation
summary: A navigation provides users with a structured and intuitive way to go to different pages, sections or features of your website or application. It tells users where they are at all times and ensures they can easily get to where they need to go. Use this pattern to provide consistency that helps users navigate your website or application easily and efficiently.

name: Navigation item
summary: Tab moves focus into the first navigation item in the vertical group. Sets focus to the entire component.

name: Navigation item
summary: Use horizontal navigation items within a horizontal group to establish a consistent and easily accessible pathway for users, while conserving valuable screen estate. This will allow users to easily scan and identify navigation options in a seamless user experience.

name: Navigation item
summary: For further details on how to use the component to provide navigation, see the navigation pattern

name: Number input
summary: Wrap NumberInput in FormField to provide the field with a visible label, help text and a status message for validation feedback. This will ensure it complies with accessibility guidelines. You can find more information in the W3C form instructions.

name: Number input
summary: The NumberInput has a default increment step of 1, which is adjustable via the step prop for precise value changes. For larger adjustments, users can hold the Shift key while using the arrow keys to apply a stepMultiplier, a prop that defaults to 2.

name: Number input
summary: To avoid misleading users, set the width to correlate to the length of the value you’re expecting. For example, an input for a three-digit value shouldn't be wide enough to accommodate a sentence worth of characters. See forms pattern for more information on layout.

name: Overlay
summary: Users expose an overlay using a focusable UI element, such as a button. On button activation by either the Enter or Space keys, focus enters the overlay.

name: Overlay
summary: The basic overlay component allows the user to expose and interact with supplemental information. The overlay remains persistent until the user dismisses it.

name: Overlay
summary: Interaction with the content in an overlay is typically constrained, as richer interactions/workflows should occur within a separate UI mechanism (such as a new page, Dialog or Drawer).

name: Overlayable characteristic
summary: Overlayable tokens define translucent styles for shadows and scrims, as well as neutral overlay layers that highlight hovered, selected, or highlighted items without masking underlying colors. This ensures that other visual cues—like zebra striping, validation states, or sentiments—remain visible and relevant. All overlayable tokens are translucent to maintain clarity across different states.

name: Overview
summary: Salt layouts are a special category of components designed to manage the overall structure and arrangement of user interface elements, rather than providing visual UI elements themselves. Layouts are responsible for organizing how other components are positioned and flow within an application or page.

name: Pagination
summary: Tab moves focus into the pagination component, setting focus to the first focusable element.

name: Pagination
summary: Use the default component to navigate a small number of pages. The user can navigate in single page increments or jump directly to a page in a set range.

name: Pagination
summary: Position the component where it’s most appropriate for your content length. On longer pages, for example, display the component both above and below content. Placing it below the content may cause frustration and excessive scrolling, and the user may not see it if it's positioned only at the top.

name: Panel
summary: This component has no accessibility guidance.

name: Panel
summary: When using panels together, use the primary variant as the background for the most important content that you want the user to focus on first.

name: Panel
summary: Pick the background that reflects the level of importance of the content (primary or secondary), which will drive the types of components displayed in the panel.

name: Parent-child layout
summary: When building a subsection of a page using ParentChildLayout, apply semantic HTML. This means using the correct HTML elements for their intended purpose as much as possible.

name: Parent-child layout
summary: A parent-child layout displays the parent component to the left and child component to the right.

name: Parent-child layout
summary: To organize content into two areas: a larger area, and a smaller area that controls the larger area.

name: Patterns
summary: Salt is a pattern-driven system. This means we provide a set of simple, high-quality, context-agnostic components and show you how to put them together in different ways, as “patterns”, to solve a specific business problem.

name: Pill
summary: When focus is on the pill, this action activates it.

name: Pill
summary: Pills are often used for quick actions such as choosing an auto-generated response to a message or reserving a seat in a room.

name: Pill
summary: To organize selections that don’t necessarily belong to the same category or need to be arranged in a certain way.

name: Preferences dialog
summary: A preferences dialog allows you to display, group and navigate application preferences within a responsive modal dialog window. This pattern introduces guidelines to make the preferences dialog consistent and usable.

name: Progress
summary: Improve accessibility by customizing the aria-label prop to provide additional context about what is loading. For example:

name: Progress
summary: Use linear or circular depending on the context, layout and functionality of an application. Use the same indicator for the same type of process to ensure consistency.

name: Progress
summary: When it’s possible to determine the length of time remaining for a task or operation to complete. This will reassure the user that it is being processed.

name: Radio button
summary: Tab moves focus to the checked radio button in the radio button group.

name: Radio button
summary: Radio button groups allow users to select one or more values from a given set of choices. You can align them horizontally or vertically.

name: Radio button
summary: When you have fewer than five options and only single selection is necessary.

name: Range date picker
summary: Wrap DatePicker in FormField to provide the field with a visible label, help text, and a status message for validation feedback. This will ensure it complies with accessibility guidelines. You can find more information in the W3C form instructions.

name: Range date picker
summary: All date components requires LocalizationProvider to be set up in your application.

name: Range date picker
summary: DatePicker provides a context to the children contained within it and a composable API that enables you to create your own date picker controls.

name: Range slider
summary: If focus is outside the RangeSlider, moves focus to the RangeSlider indicator within the tabbing order.

name: Range slider
summary: Selection of an interval of values from a RangeSlider track. A tooltip displays the value of the RangeSlider's "thumbs" when a thumb is focused or hovered.

name: Range slider
summary: When selecting a range of numeric values or relative scale.

name: Rating
summary: Tab moves focus into the rating component. Focus is set to the selected rating item.

name: Rating
summary: By default, the Rating displays five increments, as stars, from which users can select a rating.

name: Rating
summary: When you have to provide feedback or indicate your level of satisfaction with a product, service, or experience.

name: Roadmap
summary: We track all our work using GitHub issues so if you see an issue that you're interested in please leave an 👍.

name: Salt Design System
summary: Salt is J.P. Morgan's open-source design system, providing accessible components and extensive design resources to create exceptional digital experiences across lines of business.

name: Salt DS Figma Component Guides
